metadata.title: The Captive's War Character Association Dataset
metadata.sex_note: Unknown includes unstated sex, collectives, artificial entities, and alien biology not safely mapped to male/female. Clae presents as female, but the underlying Swarm is classified unknown.
metadata.spoilers: Contains major spoilers for the first two novels and Livesuit.
metadata.scope: Named and narratively significant characters; incidental unnamed background individuals are omitted.

Dafyd Alkhor.summary: Junior researcher who becomes the Carryx-appointed intermediary and plans a long resistance from within.

Tonner Freis.summary: Brilliant proteome researcher whose scientific authority is displaced by Dafyd's political authority.

Else Annalise Yannin.summary: Senior researcher, former partner of Tonner, lover of Dafyd, and host consumed by the Swarm.

Jessyn Kaul.summary: Biologist, survivor and emerging fighter who discovers the Deathless enemy's connection to humanity.

Campar.summary: Biologist, caretaker and humorist who survives hazardous Carryx military deployments.

Rickar Daumatin.summary: A compromised and later rehabilitated researcher whose death transmits the Swarm's intelligence to the Deathless.

Jellit Kaul.summary: Jessyn's astronomer brother; joins the resistance and is later consumed and impersonated by the Swarm.

Synnia.summary: Researcher whose grief over Nol turns into uncompromising resistance.

Nol.summary: Older researcher and Synnia's longtime partner, killed during the invasion.

Irinna.summary: Junior researcher and Jessyn's close friend, killed by the Night Drinkers.

Urrys Ostencour.summary: Security official who organizes armed resistance against the Carryx.

Dorinda Alkhor.summary: Dafyd's aunt, guardian and political mentor.

Llaren Morse.summary: Astronomer who helps discover the Carryx fleet and later joins the resistance.

Dennia.summary: Laser specialist and Rickar's lover, killed in the purge.

Allstin.summary: Senior astronomy researcher and resistance participant.

Merrol.summary: Astronomy department chair who views Dafyd as a possible threat to the resistance.

Samar Austad.summary: Administrator behind the attempted takeover of Tonner's project, killed by the Swarm.

Ferre Luminan.summary: One of the senior leaders in Ostencour's resistance network.

Skinnerling.summary: Engineer who manufactures resistance weapons with Kos.

Kos.summary: Engineer who manufactures resistance weapons with Skinnerling.

The Swarm / Clae Audin.summary: A Deathless spy that consumes successive hosts and eventually forms the autonomous identity Clae Audin.

Ameer Kindred.summary: The Swarm's first known host, surviving only as reconstructed memories within it.

Tkson-Malkal.summary: First Carryx keeper-librarian assigned to the human moiety.

Ekur-Tkalal.summary: Former subjugator and interrogator who becomes keeper-librarian of humanity.

The Sovran.summary: Supreme functional ruler of the Carryx, ritually killed and replaced by her daughter.

Surur-Tlassen.summary: Senior regulator and direct conduit to the Sovran who begins transitioning to creche-keeper status.

The New Sovran.summary: Daughter who kills and seamlessly replaces the reigning Sovran.

Urur-Atlak.sex_note: Explicitly a neuter remnant and former high male.
Urur-Atlak.summary: Former high male transformed into a sexless creche-keeper.

The Subjugator-Prime.summary: Military subordinate sacrificed during Ekur-Tkalal's Ayayeh campaign.

Night Drinkers' Keeper-Librarian.summary: Carryx overseer punished after the Night Drinkers lose their competition with humanity.

Garral Pär.summary: Archaeologist who deciphers the hidden humans' language and becomes a bridge to the Deathless.

Uuya Tomos.summary: Folklorist who designs a covert resistance culture for future Carryx-born humans.

Bastien Korham.summary: Infrastructure director who expands housing, agriculture, education and nursery capacity.

Llian Andermus.summary: Dafyd's severe and highly capable director of security.

Brun.summary: Tonner's deputy and successor whose work stoppage provokes Dafyd's ritual violence.

Ver Cannedan.summary: Choreographer who assaults Dafyd, then applies his expertise to reading Carryx movement.

Ghati.summary: Campar's lover and fellow military captive, later reassigned with Vaudai.

Vaudai.summary: Alien translator and tactical pattern analyst serving aboard a Carryx warship.

Dervan.summary: Anxious human captive who learns the tactical display and witnesses planetary destruction.

Danna.summary: Human captive and companion of Dervan and Emmin.

Emmin.summary: Human captive and companion of Dervan and Danna.

Corvall.summary: Armored anti-Carryx soldier who sacrifices himself to secure the refugee children's escape.

Manta.summary: Tutor and caretaker protecting ten refugee children.

Omco.summary: Language tutor whose conversations with Garral establish common human ancestry.

Carlon.summary: Deathless-associated elder who begins debriefing Garral about Anjiin.

Third Gardener.summary: Sinen administrator overseeing Jessyn's field expedition.

Farad Morse.summary: Llaren's uncle, who confronts Dafyd about Jellit's disappearance.

Ennil Day.summary: Researcher whose memory is manipulated to validate Clae's invented identity.

Kirin Foss.summary: Former medical rescue worker who volunteers for livesuit infantry and discovers that the suit progressively replaces its wearer.

Piotr.summary: Kirin's friend and fellow medic; catastrophic injuries leave a suit-operated body continuing to present as Piotr.

associations.note: Both remain behaviorally present after the original person has apparently been consumed or destroyed.

Mina.summary: Kirin's former partner, separated from him by war and time dilation, who sends a censored warning about the livesuit program.

Estebán Corval.summary: Veteran livesuit leader and mentor to Kirin; possibly connected to the similarly named Corvall in The Faith of Beasts.

associations.note: Roles and armor align, but the printed names differ by one letter and chronology is unresolved.

Deborah Ross.summary: Experienced livesuit soldier, former naval machinist and respected comrade of Kirin.

Gleaner.summary: Reliable, humorous livesuit squadmate whose reassignment demonstrates the constant erosion of wartime relationships.

Noor.summary: Member of Kirin's shifting livesuit combat team.

Simeon.summary: Livesuit officer who leads Kirin's first operational group, with Corval commanding a subordinate group.

Sergeant Huang.summary: Recruitment and orientation authority who presents the livesuit program without disclosing its irreversible consequences.

Eric Santos.summary: Talkative livesuit soldier previously known to Corval and assigned during a unit reshuffle.

workgroup_takeover_attempt.name: Attempted takeover of Tonner's project
workgroup_takeover_attempt.summary: Dyan Academy attempts to divide Tonner's team; the effort collapses after Austad's death.

anjiin_fleet_discovery.name: Discovery of the incoming fleet
anjiin_fleet_discovery.summary: Astronomers identify the anomaly that reveals the Carryx approach.

anjiin_invasion.name: Conquest of Anjiin
anjiin_invasion.summary: The Carryx conquer Anjiin, conduct a mass culling and abduct useful humans.

transport_revolt.name: Transport-ship revolt
transport_revolt.summary: Ostencour organizes an unsuccessful attack against the Soft Lothark guards.

research_trial.name: Berry/not-turtle research trial
research_trial.summary: The human team must make one captive organism nutritionally compatible with another.

night_drinker_conflict.name: Night Drinker attack
night_drinker_conflict.summary: The rival moiety attacks the human laboratory and kills Irinna.

human_retaliation.name: Human raid on the Night Drinkers
human_retaliation.summary: Jessyn leads a retaliatory raid; the Carryx later exterminate the losing moiety.

resistance_betrayal.name: Exposure of Ostencour's resistance
resistance_betrayal.summary: Dafyd and Jellit disclose the planned rebellion to prevent a wider human extermination.

carryx_purge.name: Carryx purge of the resistance
carryx_purge.summary: Rak-hund kill resistance members, including Synnia and Dennia.

swarm_transfer_to_jellit.name: Swarm transfer from Else to Jellit
swarm_transfer_to_jellit.summary: Else dies after the Swarm moves into and consumes Jellit.

ayayeh_campaign.name: Battle around Ayayeh
ayayeh_campaign.summary: Ekur discovers an enemy-manufactured trap and sacrifices most of the Carryx force.

human_intermediary_appointment.name: Dafyd appointed intermediary
human_intermediary_appointment.summary: Ekur replaces Tkson-Malkal and makes Dafyd the sole authorized human contact.

moiety_reorganization.name: Reorganization of the human moiety
moiety_reorganization.summary: Dafyd creates administrative, security, cultural and infrastructure functions.

tonner_death.name: Death of Tonner Freis
tonner_death.summary: Soft Lothark guards kill Tonner after overhearing his discovery about their behavior.

tonner_memorial.name: Tonner's memorial
tonner_memorial.summary: Uuya and Dafyd turn Tonner's remembrance into cultural resistance.

world_expedition.name: Scientific expedition to World
world_expedition.summary: Jessyn and Garral join a Carryx-directed survey of a conquered planet.

world_refugee_contact.name: Contact with World's hidden humans
world_refugee_contact.summary: Jessyn and Garral meet Corvall, Manta, Omco and the refugee children.

deathless_identity_discovery.name: Human identity of the Deathless discovered
deathless_identity_discovery.summary: Language and biological evidence reveal that Anjiin humanity and the Deathless-associated people share ancestry.

world_sabotage.name: World sabotage and escape plan
world_sabotage.summary: Corvall sacrifices himself while Jessyn smuggles a sabotage device onto a Carryx ship.

deathless_rescue.name: Rescue by the Deathless
deathless_rescue.summary: Garral and the refugees escape and establish contact with the Deathless organization.

ashtin_kah_boarding.name: Ashtin-Kah derelict boarding
ashtin_kah_boarding.summary: The captive warship team boards an enemy command vessel that failed to self-destruct.

jurupe_battle.name: Battle at Jurupe
jurupe_battle.summary: The Carryx wage genocidal warfare; Campar confronts a reanimating Deathless soldier.

swarm_transmission.name: Swarm intelligence transmission
swarm_transmission.summary: A Swarm fragment hidden in Rickar transmits intelligence during his death.

return_to_world_palace.name: Warship survivors return
return_to_world_palace.summary: Campar, Ghati and Vaudai return physically and emotionally transformed.

clae_emergence.name: Emergence of Clae Audin
clae_emergence.summary: The Swarm accepts that its hosts are dead and forms its own autonomous identity.

brun_arm_breaking.name: Dafyd's ritual correction of Brun
brun_arm_breaking.summary: Dafyd breaks Brun's arm to prevent the Carryx from treating his work stoppage as a fatal challenge.

sovran_succession.name: Carryx Sovran succession
sovran_succession.summary: A daughter kills and replaces the reigning Sovran without interrupting the empire.

two_sovrans_hypothesis.name: Two-Sovrans hypothesis
two_sovrans_hypothesis.summary: Dafyd begins considering whether competing Sovrans could fracture Carryx unity.

livesuit_enlistment.name: Kirin and Piotr enlist
livesuit_enlistment.summary: Piotr and then Kirin leave civilian rescue work for a promised eight-year livesuit tour.

livesuit_bonding.name: Permanent livesuit bonding
livesuit_bonding.summary: Recruits are encased in semibiological armor without being told that it cannot safely be removed.

first_livesuit_deployment.name: Kirin's first deployment
first_livesuit_deployment.summary: Kirin enters combat under Simeon and Corval and begins learning the suit's capabilities.

piotr_catastrophic_injury.name: Piotr's catastrophic injury
piotr_catastrophic_injury.summary: Piotr is grievously injured; the livesuit progressively replaces or operates what remains.

relativistic_separation.name: Relativistic separation from civilian life
relativistic_separation.summary: Travel and time dilation allow decades to pass outside while Kirin experiences only a few years.

egg_chamber_assault.name: Assault on the alien egg chamber
egg_chamber_assault.summary: Livesuit forces destroy a strategically important reproductive site at enormous subsequent cost.

combat_unit_reshuffling.name: Livesuit unit reshuffling
combat_unit_reshuffling.summary: Casualties and reassignment repeatedly dissolve Kirin's temporary military communities.

mina_warning.name: Mina's censored warning
mina_warning.summary: An elderly Mina sends Kirin an indirect message intended to reveal that livesuit soldiers never return home.

piotr_truth_discovered.name: Truth about Piotr
piotr_truth_discovered.summary: Kirin scans Piotr and realizes that the suit has replaced his friend to the point that Piotr is probably dead.

kirin_integration_discovered.name: Kirin discovers his own integration
kirin_integration_discovered.summary: Kirin learns that his damaged foot and much of his leg have already been replaced by livesuit material.

deathless_template.name: Deathless template hypothesis
deathless_template.summary: The Deathless may be a transmissible technological or biological pattern rather than one species.

identity_continuity.name: Identity continuity after replacement
identity_continuity.summary: The works question whether preserved behavior and memory constitute survival of the original person.

institutional_deception.name: Institutional deception
institutional_deception.summary: The livesuit program conceals permanent service while Carryx rule states its coercion openly.

time_displacement.name: Relativistic and historical displacement
time_displacement.summary: Time dilation separates livesuit soldiers from civilians, while the novella's exact distance from the novels remains unknown.

outside_inside_assimilation.name: Assimilation from outside and inside
outside_inside_assimilation.summary: Livesuits replace bodies from the exterior while the Swarm infiltrates and reconstructs hosts from within.

counterevidence: no explicit recognition or shared-history confirmation

evidence: close friend or sibling is deceived by continuity of appearance
technology reproduces the behavior of a consumed person
uncertain boundary between preserved memory and surviving self
both discover a destabilizing truth about the supposed human side of the war
both must communicate indirectly under surveillance
